name: [Portal] Terms and conditions (VOP) management in CRM: versions per language (CRM)
description:
### Summary

Partnership needs to publish and maintain the Partner Portal terms and conditions (VOP) themselves, in Czech, Slovak and Hungarian, without asking developers for a deploy. This task delivers that administration inside the internal CRM: an editor can create a new version of the terms for a language, set the date from which it applies, see at a glance which version is currently in force per language, and browse earlier versions as a read-only history. The portal itself does not touch the text directly; it asks the backend for the current version for a given language and receives the text plus its version identifier, which the acceptance flow in the follow-up task uses. Contracts, signatures and any partner-facing screen are out of scope here. The task has no hard dependency, but the login acceptance task consumes its query, so it should land first. It should fit the existing CRM terms administration where that is practical.

### Why?

The portal makes acceptance of the terms part of logging in, so the text partners see must be the version that is legally in force at that moment, and it must exist for each market language. Today there is no Partner Portal terms text at all, and Partnership must not depend on a developer and a release to publish or correct wording. Versioning with an effective-from date is what lets the portal decide whether a given user still has to accept anything. Read-only history is needed so Partnership can always say which wording a partner accepted on a given date.

### What?

In CRM, an authorised Partnership user sees a list of Partner Portal terms versions per language with their effective-from date and a clear marker of the version currently in force. They can add a new version for CZ, SK or HU, schedule it for a future date, and correct it until it becomes effective; once effective it is locked and stays in history. The backend exposes a single read query that returns, for a language, the currently effective version and its text, with defined behaviour when a language has no version yet. No partner ever sees this CRM screen; the portal display is a separate task.

### Acceptance Criteria

In CRM, a Partnership user with the right permission can create a new Partner Portal terms version for a chosen language (cs, sk, hu) with text and an effective-from date; users without the permission cannot.

The list shows all versions per language with effective-from date and marks exactly one version as current per language (the latest whose effective-from date is not in the future).

A version whose effective-from date has passed cannot be edited or deleted; a future-dated version can be edited until it becomes effective.

A query returns, for a given language, the current version's identifier, effective-from date and text; behaviour when that language has no version yet (empty result or fallback) is decided in refinement and covered by a test.

Creating a version is recorded with author and timestamp, and the history remains readable after newer versions are published.

Schema changes are delivered as migrations under 

migrations/2026/devrel/crm/

 and pass 

make lint-migrations

.

New PHP passes PHPStan level 10 (

make phpstan-l10

); the query handler and current-version selection are covered by unit tests.

### Open questions

- Wiki Q7: how the portal exposes the current VOP from CRM — one query per language, or one bundle with all three languages plus the version identifier the acceptance record needs.
- Who in Partnership owns publishing a new version and receives the CRM permission.
- One shared text translated into three languages (one version number across markets) or three independently versioned texts per market.
- Legal review of the wording that logging in constitutes acceptance is owned by legal/Partnership, not DevRel; the effective date of the first version depends on it.
- Reuse the existing CRM Terms of use administration (file-based, per-project consents) by registering a Partner Portal domain, or build a text-based variant; see Technical notes.

### Resources

- Depends on: no hard dependency; the VOP acceptance-by-login task consumes the query and is created next.
- Wiki: `DevRel_knowledgebase/wiki/projects/partner-portal.md` — Scope MVP table, row VOP; Odpovědnosti a závislosti; Q7.

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- Existing versioned terms domain to reuse or rule out: `cms/packages/Terms` (CQRS: `CreateTermCommand`, `UpdateTermCommand`, `GetTermQuery`, `GetTermsListQuery`) over `st_crm.terms_of_use` (validFrom/validUntil/visibility) and `terms_of_use_lng` (language, name, fileIdentifier). Domains register via `Shoptet\Contracts\Terms\Providers\TermDomainProviderInterface`; sole implementation `cms/packages/Logistics/Terms/LogisticDomainsProvider.php` — a partnerPortal provider would appear in the existing CRM UI.
- CRM admin UI already exists: `crm/admin/controllers/Terms/TermsController.php`, `TermsFormController.php`, templates `crm/admin/controllers/templates/Terms/`. Gap: it stores a file on CDN (`cms/packages/Terms/Adapters/CmsCdnAdapter.php`), not inline text; the portal needs renderable text, so either add a text column to `terms_of_use_lng` or store a Markdown/HTML file.
- Language fallback logic exists in `cms/packages/Terms/Service/FallbackTermService.php` (priority cs, en).
- Existing `st_crm.terms_consents` is per projectId (grantedBy/revokedBy), not per user/partner/version — acceptance recording is out of this task and needs its own model in the follow-up.
- New tables/columns go to `database/schema/st_crm.sql` via `migrations/2026/devrel/crm/` (see `migrations/AGENTS.md`; pattern `migrations/2026/devrel/crm/CZ3TDR1-572/`). Fixtures: `tests/_support/Fixtures/Terms/TermBuilder.php`.
